chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Husayn ibn Mukharrq and Abu Junadah al-Saluli, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Whoever fasts in the month of Sha'ban, he will have a purification from every slip, stain, and hastening."
Abu Hamzah said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): What is the 'stain' (wasmah)? He said: "The oath taken in disobedience [to God], and there is no vow in disobedience."
I said: What is the 'hastening' (badirah)? He said: "The oath taken in anger, and repentance from it is at the time of regret."

key_terms.بَادِرَة: Hastening or quick action, specifically an oath in anger
key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban, the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.وَصْمَة: Stain or blemish, specifically an oath in disobedience

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual benefits of fasting in Sha'ban and what specific sins does it purify one from?
ai.summary: This narration from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam elucidates the spiritual efficacy of fasting in Sha'ban as a preparatory purification for Ramadan, specifically targeting the rectification of verbal transgressions. The Imam distinguishes between 'wasmah' (oaths in disobedience) and 'badirah' (hasty oaths in anger), linking the latter to the psychological state of regret, thereby emphasizing Sha'ban as a time for introspective moral cleansing before the major fast.
